title: UI concepts, drawn
subject: How Alpine components, kits, units, patterns, parts and slots relate

brief.result: A reader can say how an Alpine component, a kit, a unit, a pattern, a part and a slot relate, and can see for any one unit which of those ties is missing.
musts: The code concepts: Alpine component and kit
The screen concepts: unit, pattern, part, frame code and slot
The markup declarations that tie the two together

ideas.title: Three territories
ideas.encounter: Code, screen and object as three regions, each concept a box with its count, each tie an arrow named by its verb.
ideas.helps: That the DOM element is where code and screen meet: components mount on it, markup declares on it.

ideas.title: Nesting dolls
ideas.encounter: The session page as nested outlines around one tapped title; numbered rings say what each repeat tap reaches, and each ring names the attribute that declares it.
ideas.helps: What a tap means at each level, and why declared levels are fewer and clearer than the DOM between them.

ideas.title: Strata
ideas.encounter: Seven bands from what is shown down to the file that draws it, with your three levels among them; a drill core on the right reads one unit through every band.
ideas.helps: How the conceptual, UI and code levels stack, and which layer a given unit is missing.

grafts: the ledger, as the second view: the same layers counted across every pattern
the tap ladder, drawn beside the Arrangement band, since it is what annotation will walk
the element named as the band where code and screen meet
selection.rationale: The strata put your three levels (the conceptual pattern, the UI kit, the Alpine component) in one order, with the declaration and the element between them, which is where they actually connect. The drill core turns the diagram into a check: pick any coded unit and read which bands it fills, as the session page shows its missing Declaration band at once. Every band and every core value can come from data/ui-units: coded.csv, instances.csv and units.csv, so the tab stays current.
assumptions: Do job and answer belong in the stack, or are they a separate question of what a unit is for?
Is Element a band a reader needs, or does it fold into Declaration?
Should the Code band read from a registry of Alpine components, which does not exist yet, rather than from built_on?
Is the core better for one unit at a time, or as columns for several units side by side?
